source.anchor: S2 centered first-order model; S3.E4-E5 actual block precision; A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1 Oracle reduction primitive; A2.Ex33-Ex35; omitted zero-residual convention.
source.original_text: Exact forward and inverse block products reconstruct the actual first-order observation of the centered quadratic potential. (f(x),\nabla f(x))=\bigl(\tfrac12\langle x,g(x)\rangle,g(x)\bigr). \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\ge4\). Set \(k=\lfloor d/n\rfloor\), \(r=d\bmod n\), and fix arbitrary actual hidden blocks \(O_1,\ldots,O_k\in O(n)\); no probability law or common determinant sign is assumed. Use the actual precision \(A=\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r)\), where \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), and the actual centered potential \(f(x)=\frac12 x^\top Ax\), with zero additive constant. Write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k,z)\) in contiguous coordinates. In Lean the zero-based embedding sends \((i,j)\) to \(jn+i\) and the residual coordinate \(i\) to \(kn+i\). The case \(r=0\) is included; it has no residual coordinates. The primitive oracle returns exact real products \(O_jv\) or \(O_j^\top v\), tagged false and true respectively. The inverse tag refers to the orthogonal block inverse, not the precision inverse. The output includes genuine Euclidean Fréchet differentiability \(\operatorname{HasGradientAt} f\ g(x)\ x\); a totalized gradient fallback is not used to establish the claim. The reconstructed block is \(g_j(x)=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}x_j-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}\bigl(Q_j^{\mathrm f}(x_j)+Q_j^{\mathrm i}(x_j)\bigr)\). Assemble \(g(x)=(g_1(x),\ldots,g_k(x),z)\); the residual is copied unchanged.

lean.statement:
∀ {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ),
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let B : Fin (d / n) → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ := fun j =>
      ((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) -
        ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) +
          (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose)
    let A := Matrix.reindex e e
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal B) 0 0
        (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ))
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
    let query : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Bool →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun j v inverse =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (if inverse then
        (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v
      else (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v)
    let xb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j))))
    let gb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      ((κ + 1) / 2) • xb x j - ((κ - 1) / 4) •
        (query j (xb x j) false + query j (xb x j) true)
    let g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) := fun x =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a => Sum.elim
        (fun ij => gb x ij.2 ij.1)
        (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))) (e.symm a))
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      HasGradientAt f (g x) x ∧
      (f x, gradient f x) = (inner ℝ x (g x) / 2, g x)
decoder_context: EuclideanSpace real (Fin m) is the real m-dimensional inner product space with the l2 norm. Fin m indexes coordinates from zero. WithLp.toLp 2 and WithLp.ofLp preserve entries; inner real is the ordinary real Euclidean inner product.

Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) real is the full group of real orthogonal matrices, containing either determinant sign. A matrix coerced from this group has inverse equal to its transpose. Matrix multiplication by a vector and the dot product are finite sums.

Matrix.reindex e e M has entries M (e.symm i) (e.symm j). Matrix.blockDiagonal B is indexed by pairs (local coordinate, block index) and vanishes between distinct blocks. Matrix.fromBlocks assembles its four displayed blocks. The symbol 1 denotes the identity matrix.

Equiv.prodComm exchanges the factors. finProdFinEquiv sends (a,b) to a times the cardinality of the second factor plus b. finSumFinEquiv concatenates the summands; finCongr transports along its displayed equality of cardinalities. Sum.elim selects the indicated branch.

HasGradientAt f v x means that f has a genuine Frechet derivative at x represented by the inner product with v. The operation gradient f x is totalized: it selects the derivative-representing vector when differentiability holds and otherwise returns zero. The displayed conjunction includes HasGradientAt as a conclusion; this context does not supply it as a premise.

Bool has the two values false and true; the displayed conditional chooses its first branch when true and its second branch when false. Scalar multiplication and real arithmetic have their usual meanings; natural division and remainder are floor division and remainder. A product equality asserts equality of both components.

reconstruction.text: For every pair of natural numbers d,n with 3 <= n <= d, every real number kappa >= 4, and every family (O_j) indexed by j = 0,...,q-1 of real orthogonal n-by-n matrices, where q = floor(d/n) and r = d mod n, the following holds. Put alpha = (kappa+1)/2 and beta = (kappa-1)/4. Identify the d coordinates with q full blocks of n coordinates followed by r remaining coordinates: the local coordinate i of block j has global coordinate j*n+i, and remaining coordinate i has global coordinate q*n+i. Define B_j = alpha I_n - beta (O_j + O_j^T), let A be the d-by-d matrix with these q diagonal blocks and the identity I_r on the remaining coordinates, with all intervening blocks zero, and define f(x) = (x^T A x)/2 on real Euclidean d-space. For v in real Euclidean n-space define Q(j,v,false) = O_j v and Q(j,v,true) = O_j^T v. For x in real Euclidean d-space, let x_j be its vector of coordinates in full block j and define g_j(x) = alpha x_j - beta (Q(j,x_j,false) + Q(j,x_j,true)). Define g(x) by placing g_j(x) in full block j and copying x on the r remaining coordinates. Then, for every x in real Euclidean d-space, f has a Frechet derivative at x represented by g(x), namely h maps to the Euclidean inner product of g(x) with h, and the simultaneous equality (f(x), gradient f(x)) = ((inner product of x with g(x))/2, g(x)) holds. In particular, the derivative and gradient assertions are conclusions for every x. The orthogonal matrices may have either determinant sign; the assertion is universal over these families.

objects.original: Euclidean real vectors and real matrices; O(n) consists of n by n real matrices O with transpose(O) O = I_n. A_O = ((κ+1)/2) I_n - ((κ-1)/4)(O+transpose(O)); the actual full precision is A_boldO = diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_(d-kn)). These are concrete matrices, not arbitrary block operators supplied by a query evaluator. The potential is f_A(x) = (1/2) x^T A x, and exact FO_A(x) is the ordered value-and-gradient pair ((1/2)x^T A x, A x). The source target is the centered Gaussian N(0,A^{-1}), but no distributional conclusion is selected here. Primitive oracle O_boldO(j,v,f) = O_j v; O_boldO(j,v,i) = transpose(O_j) v. Inverse means transpose of this orthogonal block. Query x=(x_1,...,x_k,z); each unknown block contributes g_j=((κ+1)/2)x_j-((κ-1)/4)(F_j+I_j), where F_j and I_j are the actual forward and inverse responses at the same input x_j.
objects.reconstructed: q = floor(d/n) full blocks and r = d mod n remaining coordinates; a family O_j of real orthogonal n-by-n matrices; the coordinate equivalence e with e(inl(i,j)) = j*n+i and e(inr(i)) = q*n+i; alpha = (kappa+1)/2 and beta = (kappa-1)/4; B_j = alpha I_n - beta(O_j + O_j^T); A = diag(B_0,...,B_(q-1),I_r) under e; f(x) = x^T A x/2; Q(j,v,false) = O_j v and Q(j,v,true) = O_j^T v; full-block extraction x_j; g_j(x) = alpha x_j - beta(Q(j,x_j,false)+Q(j,x_j,true)); g(x) is the assembly of g_j(x) with the unchanged remaining coordinates.
objects.evidence: Every meaning-carrying object is expanded in the statement: B_j=((κ+1)/2)I-((κ-1)/4)(O_j+O_jᵀ); A is a reindexed fromBlocks(blockDiagonal B,0,0,I_r); f=x·(Ax)/2; query is O_j v for false and O_jᵀv for true; g assembles the prescribed block expression and copies residual coordinates. The outer predicate is the genuine HasGradientAt and the actual gradient operation, not equality between two arbitrary response aliases. Whole target module and canonical singleBlockPrecision/blockPrecision definitions agree literally with the expansion and source E4/E5. Fresh exact expansion elaborates using the real theorem with no proof search beyond exact.

domains.original: The Section 2 model has integer d≥1, real κ≥1, and A symmetric with I_d ⪯ A ⪯ κ I_d; x ranges over all R^d. The selected hard-family construction stands at κ≥4, integer block dimension 3≤n≤d, k=floor(d/n), and tuple (O_1,...,O_k) in O(n)^k. Consequently d-kn is a nonnegative integer. j ranges over {1,...,k}; primitive v and every x_j lie in R^n; z lies in R^(d-kn); τ has the two meaningful tags forward f and inverse i. When kn=d, the identity block is omitted. The pointwise formula then has no residual coordinates; equivalently a zero-dimensional residual contributes the unique empty vector and zero inner-product term.
domains.reconstructed: d,n are natural numbers; kappa is real. j ranges over Fin q and full-block coordinate i over Fin n; remaining coordinate i ranges over Fin r, which may be empty. O_j belongs to the full real orthogonal group on n coordinates, allowing either determinant sign. B_j is a real n-by-n matrix, A a real d-by-d matrix, x and g(x) belong to real Euclidean d-space, and v, x_j, Q(j,v,b), and g_j(x) belong to real Euclidean n-space. The inverse selector b belongs to Bool. All inner products and derivatives are over the reals with the ordinary Euclidean inner product.
domains.evidence: hn:3≤n, hnd:n≤d, hκ:4≤κ and Os:Fin(d/n)→orthogonalGroup(Fin n)ℝ reproduce this regime. EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) and WithLp coordinate transport preserve ordinary Euclidean entries and inner product. Let q=d/n and r=d%n; Nat.div_add_mod gives q*n+r=d. Hence r=d-q*n, and the residual dimension is exactly the source dimension. Fin 0 is empty, so the residual branch disappears when n divides d. Complete blockCoordinates and library finProdFinEquiv/finSumFinEquiv definitions confirm contiguous j*n+i and q*n+i encoding; Nat.div_add_mod and Fin 0 implement the residual convention. All parameters/Os/all x retain source domains.

assumptions.original: SOURCE/STANDING: the actual hard-family precision uses exactly E4/E5 and orthogonal blocks in the source parameter regime. TYPING: real finite Euclidean coordinates, their dimensions, ordinary inner product, transpose and matrix multiplication. Exact oracle access: responses are precisely O_j x_j and transpose(O_j) x_j; no error, randomness, approximation tolerance, or noisy observations appear in the selected identities. Appendix B.1 has the ambient condition 2T<n. It is used by the ensuing indistinguishability proof, not by the algebraic reconstruction equations Ex33–35. Likewise k=floor(d/n), n≥3, κ≥4 and orthogonality specify the source family, though the displayed matrix algebra extends beyond several of those restrictions. Such an extension should be identified as an algebraic generalization, not as a source repair. No extra nonzero-vector, positive residual dimension, sign-specific determinant, Haar-randomness, Borelness, probability independence, spectral-bound witness, or pre-assumed reconstruction conclusion is required to establish these pointwise algebraic identities. The broader algorithm model has Borel requirements, but these are not additional premises of this selected pointwise result.
assumptions.reconstructed: The only displayed numerical assumptions are 3 <= n, n <= d, and 4 <= kappa. Every O_j is orthogonal by its declared domain. Thus n and d are positive and q >= 1; r is the natural remainder. The query, block extraction, matrices, function, and vector g are definitions. Differentiability and gradient correctness are not assumptions. No distributional, determinant-sign, initial-point, or nonzero-vector assumption is imposed.
assumptions.evidence: All displayed hypotheses are hn,hnd,hκ and the orthogonalGroup domain. Both query branches are exact matrix-vector definitions. HasGradientAt is in the conclusion. There is no auxiliary symmetry/regularity/consistency witness supplied as a premise. The source ambient 2T<n is absent because no T, algorithm or adaptive assertion is present. Symmetry is obtained inside the proof from the already existing canonical blockPrecision_regular; hsingle,hG,hgrad are internally proved. conclusion.original: For each block, A_Oj x_j = ((κ+1)/2)x_j - ((κ-1)/4)(O_boldO(j,x_j,f)+O_boldO(j,x_j,i)). The actual gradient of f_(A_boldO) is (A_O1 x_1,...,A_Ok x_k,z), which is reconstructed as (g_1,...,g_k,z). The identity residual passes through unchanged. The actual function value is (1/2)〈x,∇f_(A_boldO)(x)〉; hence the evaluator returns exactly the source FO ordered pair (value,gradient). In block coordinates the value is (1/2)(sum_j〈x_j,g_j〉+〈z,z〉). The expanded block expression is a consequence, not an extra source quotation. One point needs at most two primitive queries per block: the forward and inverse responses at x_j. This is 2k primitive queries across all k blocks, with no primitive query on the identity residual and no further oracle query for the value.
conclusion.reconstructed: For every x, HasGradientAt f (g(x)) x holds: f has a genuine Frechet derivative at x given by h -> <g(x),h>. At the same x, (f(x), gradient f(x)) = (<x,g(x)>/2, g(x)), asserting both f(x) = <x,g(x)>/2 and gradient f(x) = g(x). The vector g(x) uses alpha x_j minus beta times the sum of the forward and transpose query values in each full block, and equals x on the remaining coordinates.
conclusion.evidence: For every x, HasGradientAt f (g x) x is proved in the proposition, and (f x,gradient f x)=(inner ℝ x (g x)/2,g x). Given the displayed f,A,g, this asserts both real gradient correctness and actual quadratic value reconstruction. Dividing by 2 matches multiplication by 1/2 over ℝ. The source block identity is embodied by B_j and the formula for gb; the theorem states the assembled derivative/response rather than a separately named block equality. Reviewed hraw/hlin derive the actual quadratic Frechet derivative; hsingle expands actual E4, hG expands actual E5, hg transports the genuine gradient, and hval recovers actual value. Fresh production/Test/expansion all compile. Test uses actual Os1/Os2 and primitive equality at the same arbitrary x to equate real observations.

Equality to a separately invented response function without this connection would leave an unproved semantic bridge. The resource phrase is per block. This phase does not certify that adaptive reduction, its measurability, conditional Haar laws, Lemma 3.2, or the Gaussian sampling lower bound. The family index j selects a full block, the n-coordinate index i stays inside that block, and the remainder branch uses its own Fin r index. They depend only on κ. B_j depends on kappa and O_j, with size n. A and f depend on d,n,kappa and the complete family O. theorem actual_first_order_query {d n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hnd : n ≤ d)
    {κ : ℝ} (hκ : 4 ≤ κ)
    (Os : Fin (d / n) → Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
      ((Equiv.sumCongr
        ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
        (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
        (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
    let A := blockPrecision κ Os
    let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
      (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
    let query : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Bool →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun j v inverse =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (if inverse then
        (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v
      else (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v)
    let xb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j))))
    let gb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
        EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
      ((κ + 1) / 2) • xb x j - ((κ - 1) / 4) •
        (query j (xb x j) false + query j (xb x j) true)
    let g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) := fun x =>
      WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a => Sum.elim
        (fun ij => gb x ij.2 ij.1)
        (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))) (e.symm a))
    ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      HasGradientAt f (g x) x ∧
      (f x, gradient f x) = (inner ℝ x (g x) / 2, g x) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  let e : ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ≃ Fin d :=
    ((Equiv.sumCongr
      ((Equiv.prodComm (Fin n) (Fin (d / n))).trans finProdFinEquiv)
      (Equiv.refl (Fin (d % n)))).trans finSumFinEquiv).trans
      (finCongr (by simpa [Nat.mul_comm] using Nat.div_add_mod d n))
  let A := blockPrecision κ Os
  let f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ := fun x =>
    (WithLp.ofLp x) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) / 2
  let query : Fin (d / n) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → Bool →
      EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun j v inverse =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (if inverse then
      (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v
    else (Os j : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp v)
  let xb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
      EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => x (e (Sum.inl (i, j))))
  let gb : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → Fin (d / n) →
      EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) := fun x j =>
    ((κ + 1) / 2) • xb x j - ((κ - 1) / 4) •
      (query j (xb x j) false + query j (xb x j) true)
  let g : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) := fun x =>
    WithLp.toLp 2 (fun a => Sum.elim
      (fun ij => gb x ij.2 ij.1)
      (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))) (e.symm a))
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  let H : E →L[ℝ] E := Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d) A
  -- The same canonical actual-family regularity node supplies symmetry.
  have hA : A.IsHermitian := (blockPrecision_regular hn hnd hκ Os).1
  have hself : IsSelfAdjoint A := hA
  have hH : H.IsSymmetric :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.isSelfAdjoint_iff_isSymmetric.mp
      (hself.map (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin d)))
  have hf : f = fun y : E => (1 / 2 : ℝ) * inner ℝ y (H y) := by
    funext y
    dsimp only [f]
    rw [show inner ℝ y (H y) = (WithLp.ofLp y) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp y) from
      Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM A y y]
    ring
  -- Differentiate the actual quadratic; no default gradient value is used.
  have hgrad (y : E) : HasGradientAt f (H y) y := by
    have hraw := ((hasFDerivAt_id y).inner ℝ H.hasFDerivAt).const_mul (1 / 2 : ℝ)
    have hlin : (1 / 2 : ℝ) •
        ((fderivInnerCLM ℝ (y, H y)).comp ((ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E).prod H)) =
        toDual ℝ E (H y) := by
      ext v
      change (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (inner ℝ y (H v) + inner ℝ v (H y)) = inner ℝ (H y) v
      rw [← hH.apply_clm y v, (real_inner_comm v (H y)).symm]
      ring
    apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
    rw [hf, ← hlin]
    exact hraw
  let C : Matrix ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n))
      ((Fin n × Fin (d / n)) ⊕ Fin (d % n)) ℝ :=
    Matrix.fromBlocks (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => singleBlockPrecision κ (Os j)))
      0 0 (1 : Matrix (Fin (d % n)) (Fin (d % n)) ℝ)
  have hAdef : A = Matrix.reindex e e C := rfl
  intro x
  -- Ex33 is an internal actual block-action bridge, not an assumed answer.
  have hsingle (j : Fin (d / n)) : WithLp.ofLp (gb x j) =
      singleBlockPrecision κ (Os j) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp (xb x j) := by
    simp [gb, query, singleBlockPrecision, Matrix.sub_mulVec, Matrix.smul_mulVec,
      Matrix.add_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec]
  -- Recombine those block actions through the literal source coordinates.
  have hG : g x = H x := by
    ext a
    change Sum.elim (fun ij => gb x ij.2 ij.1)
      (fun i => x (e (Sum.inr i))) (e.symm a) = (A *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) a
    rw [hAdef]
    change _ = (C.submatrix e.symm e.symm *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp x) a
    rw [Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv]
    change _ = (C *ᵥ (WithLp.ofLp x ∘ e)) (e.symm a)
    generalize hz : e.symm a = z
    rcases z with ij | i
    · rcases ij with ⟨i, j⟩
      dsimp only [C]
      rw [Matrix.fromBlocks_mulVec]
      simp only [Sum.elim_inl, Matrix.zero_mulVec, add_zero]
      change (gb x j) i = (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun j => singleBlockPrecision κ (Os j)) *ᵥ
        (fun ij => x (e (Sum.inl ij)))) (i, j)
      rw [show (gb x j) i = (singleBlockPrecision κ (Os j) *ᵥ
        (fun a => x (e (Sum.inl (a, j))))) i from congrFun (hsingle j) i]
      simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Fintype.sum_prod_type, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply,
        ite_mul]
    · dsimp only [C]
      rw [Matrix.fromBlocks_mulVec]
      simp only [Sum.elim_inr, Matrix.zero_mulVec, Matrix.one_mulVec,
        zero_add, Function.comp_apply]
  have hg : HasGradientAt f (g x) x := hG.symm ▸ hgrad x
  refine ⟨hg, ?_⟩
  have hval : f x = inner ℝ x (g x) / 2 := by
    rw [hG]
    exact congrArg (fun t : ℝ => t / 2) (Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM A x x).symm
  exact Prod.ext hval hg.gradient
end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.GaussianComplexity.FirstOrderQuery

publication_context.statement: Exact forward and inverse block products reconstruct the actual first-order observation of the centered quadratic potential. (f(x),\nabla f(x))=\bigl(\tfrac12\langle x,g(x)\rangle,g(x)\bigr). \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\ge4\). Set \(k=\lfloor d/n\rfloor\), \(r=d\bmod n\), and fix arbitrary actual hidden blocks \(O_1,\ldots,O_k\in O(n)\); no probability law or common determinant sign is assumed. Use the actual precision \(A=\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r)\), where \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), and the actual centered potential \(f(x)=\frac12 x^\top Ax\), with zero additive constant. Write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k,z)\) in contiguous coordinates. In Lean the zero-based embedding sends \((i,j)\) to \(jn+i\) and the residual coordinate \(i\) to \(kn+i\). The case \(r=0\) is included; it has no residual coordinates. The primitive oracle returns exact real products \(O_jv\) or \(O_j^\top v\), tagged false and true respectively. The inverse tag refers to the orthogonal block inverse, not the precision inverse. The output includes genuine Euclidean Fréchet differentiability \(\operatorname{HasGradientAt} f\ g(x)\ x\); a totalized gradient fallback is not used to establish the claim. The reconstructed block is \(g_j(x)=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}x_j-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}\bigl(Q_j^{\mathrm f}(x_j)+Q_j^{\mathrm i}(x_j)\bigr)\). Assemble \(g(x)=(g_1(x),\ldots,g_k(x),z)\); the residual is copied unchanged.

steps.title: Identify the actual symmetric operator
steps.text: Use the same canonical actual block-family regularity theorem to obtain symmetry of A. Transfer it through the matrix-to-Euclidean continuous linear map H. The calculus uses only that symmetry; the source spectral domain remains unchanged.
steps.lean: hA consumes blockPrecision_regular. hself and hH transfer self-adjointness through Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual quadratic
steps.text: Differentiate one half of the inner product of the identity map and H. Symmetry combines the two derivative terms into the inner product with Hx. The Riesz representation gives a genuine gradient, rather than an equality involving the nondifferentiable fallback.
steps.lean: hf identifies the actual potential. hraw differentiates the inner product; hlin identifies its continuous linear derivative with toDual ℝ E (H y); hgrad concludes HasGradientAt.

steps.title: Reconstruct each actual block action
steps.text: Expand the literal source matrix. Its action on the queried block is exactly the stated affine combination of the two actual primitive replies. This identity is proved internally for every block.
steps.lean: hsingle uses the actual singleBlockPrecision definition and matrix sub/smul/add action identities. No gradient, symmetry or block-action answer is a public premise.

steps.title: Reassemble the actual global gradient
steps.text: Transport through the literal contiguous-coordinate equivalence, expand the block diagonal action and preserve the residual identity action. This includes the zero-dimensional residual without imposing a positive-remainder hypothesis.
steps.lean: hAdef identifies the canonical blockPrecision with its literal reindexing. hG uses submatrix_mulVec_equiv, fromBlocks_mulVec, finite block sums and hsingle; hg transports hgrad.

steps.title: Recover the value and the observation
steps.text: The same actual quadratic has value one half of its inner product with the reconstructed vector. Combine that equality with the genuine gradient. The focused consumer compares two actual hidden tuples whose primitive replies agree at the same point, then deduces equality of both actual observations.
steps.lean: hval uses Matrix.inner_toEuclideanCLM; Prod.ext hval hg.gradient concludes. Tests.GaussianComplexityFirstOrderQuery uses the theorem twice and congruence of the actual affine reply combination.
